constraints.description: Applications must be made jointly by the researcher and a beneficiary in the academic or non-academic sector.

European Postdoctoral Fellowships are open to researchers of any nationality who wish to engage in R&I projects by coming to Europe from any country in the world or moving within Europe. The standard duration must be between 12 and 24 months.

Global Postdoctoral Fellowships are open to European nationals or long-term residents wishing to engage in R&I with organisations outside EU/Associated Countries. They require an outgoing phase of minimum 12 and maximum 24 months in a non-associated Third Country, plus a mandatory 12-month return phase to an EU/Associated Country host organisation.

Postdoctoral Fellowships may include an additional period of up to six months for a placement in an organisation from the non-academic sector established in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country, to be taken at the end of the project.

The request for a non-academic sector placement must be an integral part of the proposal, explicitly explaining the added value for the project and for the career development of the researcher, and is subject to separate evaluation.

If the non-academic placement does not meet requirements (e.g., takes place in an academic organisation or in a Third Country), the proposal will be evaluated without taking into account the placement. This might affect the final score.

For European Postdoctoral Fellowships, secondments cannot exceed half of the requested duration of the action (excluding any additional non-academic placement period) and should be in line with project objectives, adding significant value and impact to the fellowship.
Secondments cannot take place during the mandatory twelve-month return period to the host organisation in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country (applies to Global Fellowships).

Training activities must integrate key transferable skills and competences common to all fields, including digital skills (e.g. generative AI), and must foster the culture of Open Science, knowledge valorisation, innovation and entrepreneurship where applicable, and good scientific conduct including research integrity.

A Career Development Plan covering research objectives, training and career needs (including transferable skills, teaching, publications, conferences, and Open Science activities) must be established jointly by the supervisor(s) and the researcher, and submitted as a project deliverable at the beginning of the action.
Specific eligibility conditions apply to MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships in research areas covered by the Euratom Research and Training Programme (described at the end of the Work Programme part).

Admissibility conditions are described in Annex A and Annex E of the Horizon Europe Work Programme General Annexes. Proposal page limits and layout are described in Part B of the Application Form available in the Submission System.

The call operates under a single-stage deadline model with submission deadline of 2026-09-09. Award criteria, scoring thresholds, submission and evaluation process, and indicative timeline are described in the Horizon Europe Work Programme General Annexes (Annex D, Annex F) and the Online Manual.
